statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail sits far below the block threshold because CME equity-index futures have been in their weekend halt since Friday 21:00Z and no NQ price path exists to score, while Stress stays elevated on the carried-in rate, energy and Gulf-supply backdrop.

headline: Weekend halt pins Tail at 3 as Friday's record probe stays fully retraced and the Riyadh refinery fire remains unattributed
body: Friday 2 October remains the last traded session before the halt. The Nasdaq-100 closed at a record 30,807.93, up 306.37 points or 1.00%, after a soft September employment report showed 29,000 jobs added against about 90,000 expected, unemployment at 4.2% and average hourly earnings up 0.1% on the month, with August revised down to 133,000 from 162,000. The structurally decisive detail for this framework is that the new intraday record at 31,017.53 was fully retraced into a close near the 30,737.07 session low. That is orderly mean reversion, not the shallow-pullback extension or failed-retracement pattern that defines Tail, so Tail holds at 3 across the whole window. VIX closed at 15.31, down 6.59%, with a 15.30-16.24 range. Stress is 58 and drifts to 63 across the window on the carried-in environment rather than on observed structure: Treasury yields reversed upward despite the soft print, with the 2-year at 4.84%, the 10-year at 5.28% after an intraday 5.34% high described as the strongest since 2002, and the 30-year at 5.61%. Brent settled at $102.25, down 0.06% on the day but up 7.05% on the month and 58.45% on the year, having jumped about 4% on Thursday on reporting of a third U.S. carrier strike group heading to the region; the EIA's September outlook still assumes constrained Middle East flows with fourth-quarter shut-ins averaging about 5.7 million barrels a day. Fire and a smoke plume were reported on Saturday morning at Aramco's Riyadh refinery, a roughly 130,000 barrel-a-day asset, with satellite thermal detections cited in reporting; as of this assessment neither Saudi authorities nor Aramco had confirmed the incident or a cause, no group had claimed responsibility, and no damage, casualties or production impact had been reported, so it is treated as an unresolved Stress and Confidence input rather than a priced supply shock. Confidence is 83: the index level and session range, volatility, the full yield curve, Brent, and the seven-day U.S. calendar were each verified from primary or authoritative current sources, and the single material open item is the unexplained Riyadh fire. The shared Finviz context file was 90 hours old and marked partial, so it was discarded and the assessment rests on independent research. No futures price discovery is available anywhere inside this forecast window.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry published Claude assessments. The window opens in Friday's post-payroll U.S. session with Tail 22-23 and Stress 78-79 under a mixed mode, then decays steadily after the 21:00Z futures close: Tail falls from 14 to 3 and Stress from 74 to 52 across the overnight and Saturday hours, with the mode settling to normal from 00:00Z. The last five hours sit flat at Tail 3 while Stress edges back from 52 to 57 as the Gulf energy thread reopened.
outlookSummary: Every hour of this forecast window falls inside the CME equity-index weekend halt, so no NQ price path can form and Tail is held flat at 3, mapping to EA_ON and green throughout. Stress drifts from 58 to 63 because unresolved Gulf-supply and rate threads accumulate without a venue able to price them, and Confidence eases from 83 to 78 as Friday's verified levels age. The one genuinely differentiating interval is the Saudi Exchange session from 07:00Z to 12:00Z on 4 October, the only open market relevant to the refinery incident; under the delayed-evidence rule it can inform Stress and Confidence but cannot establish current Nasdaq-100 structure. The CME restart at 22:00Z on 4 October lies about six hours past the final scored hour, so the first genuine post-weekend price-path evidence, and any restart gap, falls outside this horizon.
